properties.decision:
ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-10: *"agreed on the 'behavioural rather than lexical' approach."*

SETTLED: if repeated attention to a node is ever used as a priority signal, the unit of evidence is that a search surfaced the node AND the agent then FETCHED IT IN FULL. Not the BM25 score, not the appearance in a ranked list.

WHY THIS AXIS COULD BE SETTLED WHILE THE REST STAYS OPEN. The lexical route was measured and found unusable in the form anybody would reach for: `search_design` returns BM25, which is unbounded and query-dependent — the query "export" scored its top hit at 4.48 and a longer query on the same subject scored 35.75, eight times higher for the same topic. Any accumulation of raw scores weights verbose queries over terse ones and would drift with whoever (or whatever model) writes the query. A behavioural unit needs no score at all, so it sidesteps comparability entirely and cannot be gamed by query length.

⭐ ANTHONY'S FRAMING, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN DECORATIVE: *"this is a bit like a Q-table in reinforcement learning... the more that a search appears, the more that it is reinforced."* Three consequences follow from taking that seriously, and none of them is obvious from the counter idea alone.

(1) A Q-VALUE DECAYS AND A COUNTER DOES NOT. Reinforcement learning applies a learning rate precisely so that recent evidence outweighs old; a plain tally never forgets. Without decay, whatever was hot in a project's first month dominates its ranking forever, and a node read ten times in July and never since reads as more critical than one read three times this week. ⇒ IF THIS IS BUILT, RECENCY IS PART OF THE UPDATE RULE, NOT A LATER REFINEMENT.

(2) VISIT COUNT IS NOT VALUE. In a Q-table the update is driven by REWARD; the visit count is exploration bookkeeping. "Searched often" is a visit count. What Anthony actually wants is closer to Q — did going there PAY OFF — and that is the deeper argument for the behavioural unit he chose: choosing to read a node in full is a weak revealed preference, where appearing in a list is not even that.
⚠️ THE ANALOGY BREAKS HERE AND THE BREAK MUST BE RECORDED: THERE IS NO REWARD SIGNAL. Nothing observes whether reading a node helped. The agent's choice to read is a proxy for relevance, not a measurement of outcome, and treating it as reward would assert an observation nobody makes. The RL framing supplies STRUCTURE (decay, exploration) and does NOT supply the thing that makes Q-learning converge.

(3) 🛑 THE EXPLORATION TRAP, AND IT IS `dec:bl-155` ARRIVING BY A NEW ROAD. A reinforcement scheme reinforces what has already been visited. A node nothing surfaces is never read, so it never accumulates, so it never rises — permanently. That is exactly bl-155's finding that reflow2 cannot tell "unused" from "unreachable", and `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` already drew the consequence that counts may justify optimising and never, alone, justify cutting. THE RL FRAMING ADDS THE REMEDY SHAPE THAT THE EARLIER FRAMING LACKED: greedy exploitation of an under-explored table converges on a local optimum, and the standard answers are an exploration term or optimistic initialisation. ⇒ ANY ATTENTION RANKING NEEDS A DELIBERATE EXPLORATION COMPONENT — something that surfaces never-touched nodes on purpose — or it will bury exactly the material a discoverability problem is already hiding. Recorded as a REQUIRED PROPERTY of any such design, not as a nice-to-have.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, and `dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important` stays OPEN for all of it: whether attention should be tracked at all; where the record lives (`dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` holds that); how it composes with ranking by CONSEQUENCE (`dec:idea-a-critical-path-through-the-undecided`); and whether a bounded top-5 draws from one merged score or two lists. This decision closes one axis so the others can be argued without re-litigating it.

STILL BINDING FROM THE OPEN NODE: the search history is LOCAL BY CONSTRUCTION and never enters a telemetry payload — `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` governs what LEAVES a design and names search queries as the worst offender. And review records and bookkeeping must be excluded from any accumulation, per the exclusion list `fact:graph-analysis-covers-a-third-of-the-edge-types` had to learn the expensive way.
properties.name: Attention is measured by what was READ, not by what a search scored — behavioural, not lexical
properties.rationale:
Recorded as its own accepted Decision rather than by editing the brainstorm node into an answer, per `dec:reopen-supersedes`' principle that the record should show both that a question was asked and how it was settled. It deliberately does NOT obsolete `dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important`: Anthony settled the lexical-versus-behavioural axis, not whether to build any of this, so superseding the whole question would claim more than he said.

The Q-table framing is recorded as design content rather than as a metaphor because it produces three testable properties the counter idea did not have — decay, the visit-count-is-not-value distinction, and an exploration term — and because its BREAK is as informative as its fit: there is no reward signal here, and an implementation that pretended otherwise would be asserting an observation nobody makes.

Consequence (3) is the one worth carrying forward. bl-155's unused-versus-unreachable finding has been restated three times in this design as a warning; the RL framing is the first time it has arrived with a known remedy shape attached.
